podcast.title: Backed Elvis Costello
podcast.body: Members of this California band provided the backing for Elvis Costello on his 1977 debut album, *My Aim Is True*, as he had not yet formed his own backing band. "He was backed by members of the California band Clover, who would regroup in the 80s as the chart topping band Huey Lewis and The Newt."

podcast.title: Backing Elvis Costello's Debut
podcast.body: Clover, an American band residing in London, served as the backing band for Elvis Costello's debut album, "My Aim Is True." They were specifically hired by Stiff Records for the sessions, with their singer (Huey Lewis) being the only member not to participate, merely observing. "The real name of the Sham Rocks was actually Clover, and they were a bunch of Americans living in London who had some extra time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

podcast.title: Evolution into Huey Lewis and the News
podcast.body: After recording with Elvis Costello, Clover returned to the United States and subsequently changed their name, becoming the well-known band Huey Lewis and the News. This means Costello's first backing band was essentially Huey Lewis and the News, without Huey himself on vocals for those sessions. "Once the recording sessions wrapped up, Clover went back to the States and changed their name. You may have heard of them. Huey Lewis in the news."

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Member Destinies
podcast.body: After Clover broke up in 1978, its members pursued various paths. One individual joined The Doobie Brothers before eventually quitting music to become a chiropractor. Another member achieved recognition by writing the song "867-5309/Jenny" for Tommy Tutone. Additionally, two members, along with Clover's singer (who had merely hung around during the Elvis Costello sessions), went on to form the successful band Huey Lewis and the News. "Clover broke up in 1978. One guy joined the Dubie Brothers before quitting music to become a chiropractor, and another guy wrote the song 867-5309-Geni for Tommy Tutone."

podcast.title: Pseudonym for American Clover
podcast.body: The Sham Rocks was a pseudonym adopted by the American band Clover when they were working in the UK. This was done to avoid legal trouble, as there was already an existing British band named Clover. Under this name, they famously backed Elvis Costello on his debut album, My Aim Is True, although they remained uncredited. "This is because there was already a British band called Clover, so the American Clover tried to use the name, the Sham Rocks, to avoid getting in trouble."

podcast.title: Uncredited Backing Band for Elvis Costello
podcast.body: Clover was an American band that found itself broke while touring the UK. They were hired by Jake Riviera of Stiff Records to back Elvis Costello on his debut album, My Aim Is True, recording through late 1976 and early 1977 in a tiny studio in Islington, London. Due to contractual issues (another British band was already named Clover), they used the pseudonym The Sham Rocks and were never credited on the original album release. "So Riviera found a band called Clover, who had come over from America, and were pretty much broke as they tried to or the UK."

xref.title: My Aim Is True (1977) – Debut Album Recorded by Clover, Who Became Huey Lewis and the News
xref.body: Before his music career, Elvis Costello worked as a computer operator for Elizabeth Arden cosmetics, running invoices on an IBM 360 mainframe, taking occasional sick days to demo songs. When he signed to Stiff Records, he needed a backing band. An American group called Clover had just arrived in England hoping for their big break, but found themselves stranded in the middle of punk and unwanted. They needed money for plane tickets home. Elvis went to their residency at Headley Grange, told them he needed a studio band and specifically didn't need a singer, so Clover's own singer was sent to wait elsewhere while the rest of the band backed Elvis through six four-hour sessions for his debut. Clover was paid and sent back to the US, where they reinvented themselves as Huey Lewis and the News. The singer who had to hang out during the Costello sessions was Huey Lewis. "That banished singer was Huey Lewis."

xref.title: Clover's Transformation into Huey Lewis and the News
xref.body: The band Clover provided backup instrumentation for Elvis Costello's debut album, *My Aim is True*, performing under the name The Shamrocks. After their work with Costello, and once he had auditioned players for his permanent group (The Attractions), Clover returned to the United States and subsequently changed their name to Huey Lewis and the News, becoming the well-known band.

xref.title: Early Backup Band (Clover/The Shamrocks)
xref.body: Stiff Records expedited the release of Elvis Costello's debut album, *My Aim is True*, and due to time constraints, a permanent band could not be assembled. Jake Riviera, the head of Stiff, brought in a touring group named Clover to provide instrumentation for Costello's acoustic demos at Pathway Studios. They played under the name The Shamrocks for the official contract to avoid being sued by another band called Clover.

xref.title: Formation for Second Album
xref.body: The Attractions were formed by Elvis Costello for his second album because Clover (his backing band for "My Aim Is True") was unavailable and "lacked a certain intensity." The band consisted of "music industry vets." "That's when Elvis Gustell finally formed his own group. The attractions were made up of some music industry vets and they would join Elvis off and on over the next couple of decades."

xref.title: Huey Lewis and the News as Backing Band (Clover)
xref.body: For his debut album, "My Aim Is True," Elvis Costello, then a solo singer, was backed by a band called The Sham Rocks. The Sham Rocks were actually Clover, a group of Americans living in London, with the notable exception of their singer, who simply observed the sessions. After recording, Clover returned to the United States and later gained fame as Huey Lewis and the News, meaning Costello's first backing band was essentially Huey Lewis and the News minus Huey. "The real name of the Sham Rocks was actually Clover, and they were a bunch of Americans living in London who had some extra time."

xref.body: Huey Lewis and the News was formed by two members of the American band Clover, along with Clover's singer. These individuals had previously played an uncredited but significant role as the backing band on Elvis Costello's debut album, My Aim Is True, performing under the pseudonym The Sham Rocks. "And two guys, plus that singer who had been hanging around in the lobby, formed a new band called Huey Lewis in the News."

xref.body: The Attractions became Elvis Costello's crack backup band, but they did not form until his second album. His debut album, My Aim Is True, was recorded with a different, uncredited American band called Clover (performing as The Sham Rocks). "But that band didn't come together until the second album."
